facts.text: Rover Wheel Tracks was deployed at Gusev Crater during Spirit (MER-A) in 2006.

Spirit's broken right front wheel, which stopped turning in 2006, inadvertently became a scientific tool. As Spirit dragged the wheel, it scraped away the surface layer to reveal bright white soil rich in silica — up to 90% pure SiO₂. This discovery suggested either hot springs or fumaroles once existed here.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Accidentally uncovered soil that was 90% pure silica — a composition that on Earth forms only in hot springs or volcanic steam vents.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Gusev Crater.
The wheel tracks exposing silica remain on the surface, a visible record of one of Mars exploration's most serendipitous discoveries.
